items.title: Thanksgiving Monday: What’s Open and Closed in Toronto and Southern Ontario
items.summary: Thanksgiving Monday is here, and many stores, businesses, government offices and services will be closed or operating on reduced hours across Toronto and southern Ontario today. Thanksgiving falls on Monday, Oct. 12, 2026, with closures and holiday hours expected in Toronto, Mississauga, Brampton, Hamilton, Halton, Durham, Niagara and other cities and towns across Ontario. Thanksgiving has been officially celebrated as an annual holiday in Canada since Nov. 6, 1879 and is traditionally observed on the second Monday in October. In 1957, Governor General Vincent Massey issued a proclamation establishing the second Monday in October as a day of thanksgiving for Canada’s annual harvest. Thanksgiving is a statutory holiday in Ontario and most of Canada, although its status differs in Prince Edward Island, Newfoundland and Labrador, Nova Scotia and New Brunswick. Here’s a look at what’s open and closed on Thanksgiving Monday in: In Mississauga, a number of places will be open Oct. 12, including Square One Shopping Centre (including the Walmart Supercentre, Food District and Rec Room locations in the mall), Whole Foods Square One, T&T Supermarket, most cafes, restaurants and bars that are typically open on Mondays (call ahead to confirm), some smaller grocery stores (such as Rabba locations), most Shoppers Drug Mart locations, YMCA locations, movie theatres and most gas stations and convenience stores. All government offices at all levels of government, including City Hall, will be closed.

items.title: Mississauga Rebels win 2026 Wendy Dufton Memorial - Ontario Hockey League
items.summary: The Mississauga Rebels captured the 2026 Wendy Dufton Memorial U16 AAA Tournament championship in dramatic fashion on Sunday, scoring with just 13 seconds remaining in regulation before defeating Detroit’s Victory Honda 2-1 in a shootout at Western Fair Sports Centre in London. Trailing 1-0 in the closing moments of the championship game, Mississauga found the equalizer to force overtime. Following a scoreless extra period, Mateo Georgy and Liam Kozlowski converted their shootout attempts for the Rebels, while goaltender David Stewart stopped Luke Rowe before Anthony Shipway’s attempt missed the net, securing the tournament title. The Rebels reached the championship game following a 2-1 semifinal victory over the North York Rangers earlier Sunday, completing a memorable four-day run against some of the top U16 AAA competition from across North America. Hosted by the London Junior Knights from October 8-11, the annual tournament brought together 40 U16 AAA teams from Ontario and the United States, providing an important early-season showcase for players eligible for the 2027 OHL Priority Selection. Several prospects delivered standout offensive performances throughout the tournament, with Honeybaked forward Landon Burke leading all players with 14 points (11-3–14) in seven games. Burke also finished as the tournament’s leading goal scorer with 11, including five goals and seven points in three playoff contests. Upper Canada College Blues forward Isaya Papineau finished tied for second in scoring with 12 points (6-6–12) in five games, having led all players with 11 points through the round-robin portion of the event. Honeybaked’s Zach Wade also recorded 12 points (3-9–12) in seven games, leading the tournament with nine assists. Georgy paced the championship-winning Rebels with 11 points (6-5–11) in eight games, while teammates Max Kopec and Gavin Laughlin each contributed nine points (4-5–9).

items.title: Mississauga mayor’s race gets heated. Here is what you need to know if you have missed the fireworks
items.summary: A heated mayoral race is shaping up in Mississauga, where observers could be forgiven for thinking it bares some resemblance to a telenovela. To understand the players, one has to back up a little bit to 2024. After holding the mayor’s office for 10 years, Bonnie Croimbie stepped down from the role after winning the leadership of the Ontario Liberal Party. In the wake of Crombie’s departure, longtime councillor Carolyn Parrish won a byelection to replace her. Months after losing the provincial election in February 2025, Crombie said she would step down as leader of the party. She announced this past summer that she would run to get her old job back as mayor of Mississauga. However Parrish, the now-incumbent mayor, is running to hold onto her job. The 80-year-old is seeking a second term. In total, there are 14 candidates running for mayor. Among them, other frontrunners include Ward 2 councillor Alvin Tedjo and Ward 7 councillor Dipika Damerla. There was no love lost between Crombie and Parrish at a recent mayoral debate, where voices were raised, eyes rolled and insults flew. Parrish referred to Crombie as “the blond bombshell” and claimed staff were “terrified” she would return. Crombie retorted staff were in fact terrified of Parrish and accused her of sitting in her office rather than going out to do the job of mayor.

items.title: New Poll Finds Younger and Older Mississauga Voters Split Sharply Over Hazel McCallion's Legacy
items.summary: According to a new Liaison Strategies survey, Hazel McCallion's legacy carries far more weight with older Mississauga voters than with younger ones heading into the mayoral race. The poll found 75 per cent of residents 65 and older say her legacy matters when picking a mayor, compared with just 29 per cent of those aged 18 to 34. Liaison reports the finding stands out as incumbent Mayor Carolyn Parrish and former mayor Bonnie Crombie defend their records against councillors Alvin Tedjo and Dipika Damerla, framing the race as a contest between experience and change. Overall, the survey found 49 per cent of residents call McCallion's legacy important, even as 52 per cent say a candidate claiming to have learned from her wouldn't change their vote. Liaison Strategies says it surveyed 1,000 Mississauga residents by phone between Oct. 2 and Oct. 4 using interactive voice recording technology, weighting the results to match 2021 Census targets. Liaison Strategies principal David Valentin said the campaign has become an argument over who can best lead the city, whether that's the sitting mayor, a returning former mayor, or a councillor promising change.

items.title: Decades of City Hall Experience Collide in Mississauga's Four-Way Mayoral Race
items.summary: According to the Pointer, Mississauga's next mayor will take on outsized powers at a moment when affordability, housing and growing congestion are testing the city's limits for its more than 800,000 residents. The outlet reports crime has also risen to the top of the City Hall agenda heading into the vote. The Pointer profiles four front-running candidates: councillors Alvin Tedjo and Dipika Damerla, incumbent Mayor Carolyn Parrish and former mayor Bonnie Crombie. The outlet notes Tedjo and Damerla both challenged Parrish in the 2024 mayoral by-election that first put her in office, while Crombie is seeking a return to the job she held for more than nine years before leaving to lead the Ontario Liberals. The Pointer reports Damerla brings nearly eight years on council and seven years as a provincial MPP for Mississauga, while Tedjo has served roughly four years at the council level. According to the outlet, all four candidates are centering their campaigns on affordability, crime and transportation, with Damerla also making City Hall accountability a signature issue.

items.title: Mississauga's Next Hospital Carries a $1-Billion Price Tag, and Fundraisers Are Two-Thirds There
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, Trillium Health Partners Foundation has launched a $1-billion fundraising campaign called Built for Us to help build what's billed as Canada's largest hospital, the future Peter Gilgan Mississauga Hospital. The outlet reports the new facility will replace the existing Mississauga Hospital and include the Shah Family Hospital for Women and Children, described as the province's first hospital dedicated specifically to women's and children's health. Foundation president and CEO Caroline Riseboro told Mississauga.com the campaign builds on funding already committed by the province and the City of Mississauga, plus transformational support from private donors. Riseboro said the foundation has raised about $600 million so far and is aiming to close the remaining $400 million gap by 2032. Mississauga.com reports the Peter Gilgan Mississauga Hospital is expected to open in late 2033 or early 2034.

items.title: A Mississauga Ticket-Holder Says She's Heard Nothing a Month After a Comedy Festival Fell Through
items.summary: According to CTV News Toronto, ticket-holder Brenna Oude-Reimerink says she still hasn't gotten a refund a month after the Great Outdoors Comedy Festival was abruptly postponed. The outlet reports the festival was scheduled to run Sept. 11 to 13 at Erindale Park near the University of Toronto Mississauga, with headliners including Stavros Halkias, John Mulaney and Jeff Arcuri. CTV News Toronto says Oude-Reimerink paid roughly $394 for two VIP tickets through a third-party ticket seller, expecting exclusive entry lanes and table service. She told the outlet she and her sister had been especially excited to see Arcuri perform live for the first time. CTV News Toronto reports organizers sent a detailed logistics email on Sept. 7, then abruptly announced the postponement the very next day without giving a clear reason. The outlet says festival organizers offered only a brief public statement calling the postponement the right call to deliver the best possible festival.

items.title: Three-Way Mayoral Race Pits a 15-Year Rivalry Against a Rising Outsider in Mississauga
items.summary: According to the Toronto Star, Mississauga's mayoral race has turned into one of the tightest and most closely watched in the city's recent history. The outlet reports incumbent Mayor Carolyn Parrish took the job after Bonnie Crombie stepped down to run for Ontario Liberal leader, finally realizing what the Star describes as a decades-old ambition to lead the city. The Star says Crombie, who first succeeded longtime mayor Hazel McCallion, is now trying to win the seat back and is invoking McCallion's legacy as she mounts her comeback following a failed bid to unseat Premier Doug Ford. The outlet reports councillor Alvin Tedjo, whose Chinese-Indonesian parents settled in downtown Mississauga when he was four, started the race trailing colleague Dipika Damerla in the polls but has since moved ahead of her as the race's generational-change candidate. Councillor Brad Butt, a Parrish supporter, told the Star the contest remains very fluid heading into the vote.

items.title: Peel Region's South Asian Film Festival Marks 15 Years With a Shift Toward Local Talent
items.summary: According to CBC, the International Film Festival of South Asia is celebrating its 15th year as a Peel Region cultural institution. The outlet reports the anniversary marks a turning point for the festival, which started out curating films from around the world and is now building an ecosystem meant to help local South Asian filmmakers get their work made and seen. CBC Peel's Nav Nanwa hosted this year's gala on Friday in Brampton, a city that sits alongside Mississauga in the heart of the GTA's South Asian community. Nanwa spoke with organizers and attendees before taking the stage, gathering their reflections on how far the festival has come. CBC says the milestone event highlights the growing presence of homegrown South Asian filmmaking talent across the region.

items.title: Mississauga Mayoral Candidate Channels Bollywood to Promise No Property Tax Hike
items.summary: According to the Deccan Chronicle, Mississauga mayoral candidate Dipika Damerla is drawing attention in Ontario's municipal election with a campaign video built around a reworked Bollywood song. The outlet reports Damerla, born in Secunderabad, completed her MBA in Toronto before winning election to Mississauga city council in 2018. She went on to serve seven years as the Ontario Liberal MPP for Mississauga East-Cooksville, including time as associate minister for long-term care and later as minister responsible for seniors affairs. The Deccan Chronicle says Damerla worked in corporate banking and ran her own business in Mississauga before entering politics. In the video shared on X, she sings a modified version of the Bollywood song 'Kya Hua Tera Wada' and pledges that property taxes will not rise if she becomes mayor. The outlet reports the video closes with her campaign slogan, 'A city that works,' alongside an appeal for voter support. The City of Mississauga's own website confirms Damerla served as the Ward 7 councillor beginning in 2018.
